newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU agrees to advance beef sector payments.
newsitem.headline: EU agrees to advance beef sector payments.

text.p: The European Commission approved on Wednesday advance payments of about 500 milion ecus worth of beef premia from the 1996 budget which are due in 1997, a Commission offical said.
"The Commission has adopted the proposal which will be put to the beef management committee on Friday (September 27)," the official said.

The draft regulation (amending regulation EEC No 3886/92) will, after the management committee has given its opinion, be published on or before October 1 to permit payment from that date, the official said.
The advances in the beef and veal sector allows for an increase in the amount of the advance payment of the beef special premium and of the suckler cow premium in addition to earlier payment.

The amended regulation states that "the advance on the special (beef) premium and on the suckler cow premium in respect of the 1996 calender year may be paid from 1 October 1996 for an amount up to 80 percent of those premia."

The decision, which will come into force on the day it is published in the EU Official Journal, will give the Commission an additional 500 million Ecus in 1997 which farm ministers meeting in Killarney on Monday said they want used to provide additional aid to the beef sector.
The decision reflects a German led view among ministers that the Commission's plan's to cut arable area aid and setaside aid payments are unecessary, the official said.

A decision on Agriculture Commissioner Franz Fischler's package of measure to reform the beef sector which he says will cost 1.3 billion ecus was deferred at this month's farm ministers' meeting because the European Parliament had not given an opinion.
The package will be discussed by ministers at the next farm ministers meeting in Luxembourg in October.
